That catalogue mix is the Deputy setup filter — not a generic hr lecture.

Buyer question: is Deputy the right hr commit for Multi-location hourly operators who need scheduling + time + labor compliance, or is Tiny shops that need a free ≤10-employee plan the real constraint?

Thesis for setup: Deputy is a yes only when applicant tracking plus core hris (Lite, Core, Pro) are must-haves; not worth it if Tiny shops that need a free ≤10-employee plan dominates the operating model.

Best for: Multi-location hourly operators who need scheduling + time + labor compliance; Teams that will trial Core for up to 31 days before Homebase-style SMB hubs; Ops leaders who want WFM AI with a human-in-the-loop (Multi-location hourly operators who need scheduling + time + labor compliance).

Poor fit when: Tiny shops that need a free ≤10-employee plan; Restaurant groups standardised on 7shifts; Buyers whose primary job is core HRIS or structured ATS. Avoid if Every user including managers is billed; list price invoice minimum would block go-live.

sections.heading: Deputy limitation, pricing interpretation, and alternative context
sections.body:
Limitation: Every user including managers is billed; list price invoice minimum; HR, analytics, messaging, and US payroll are add-ons (some bundled on Pro); SMS is usage-priced by country because it forces process changes or add-ons around Deputy when applicant tracking is the job.

Pricing interpretation: no free plan confirmed — scope a paid pilot on Lite with exit criteria before annual seats.

Plan trade-off: you gain core hris (Lite, Core, Pro) at the expense of Published free tiers vs paid depth for ATS, WFM, time, or training jobs — measure both in the pilot. Researched packaging: Lite · applicant tracking | Core | Pro.

Alternative context: unlike Connecteam, Deputy is preferable when Multi-location hourly operators who need scheduling + time + labor compliance because applicant tracking plus core hris (Lite, Core, Pro) match; prefer Connecteam when Tiny shops that need a free ≤10-employee plan because the operating loops differ.

sections.heading: Decision scenario and conclusion for Deputy
sections.body:
Use-case: for Multi-location hourly operators who need scheduling + time + labor compliance running applicant tracking, prefer Deputy when applicant tracking is weekly; pick another path when Tiny shops that need a free ≤10-employee plan.

Setup requires a specialist owner when Every user including managers is billed; list price invoice minimum collides with applicant tracking; SMB pilots can stay lighter if core hris (Lite, Core, Pro) is already on Lite.

Integrations in research: Slack, Google Workspace.

Wrap: choose Deputy only if the setup job is applicant tracking under Multi-location hourly operators who need scheduling + time + labor compliance; otherwise use Finder constraints instead of copying this page for another vendor.
